resolutions.background: This wording is quite ambiguous and does not specify the cases where z-index is not eligible.
irc: <fantasai> smfr: Issue about whether will-change: z-index triggers a stacking context
<fantasai> ... some ambiguity about if 'position' allows index, will it kick in
<fantasai> ... more complex is will-change: position, z-index
<fantasai> ... but position itself will create a stacking context
<flackr> q+
<fantasai> ... so maybe not much except spec clarification?
<JohnJansen> ack flackr
<fantasai> flackr: for the more general case, I would suggest being more pessimistic
<fantasai> ... e.g. if this property in combination with another value would have an effect, take that effect
<fantasai> smfr: [missed]
<fantasai> flackr: For each individual property, does it sometimes have that effect, even if it doesn't currently
<fantasai> ... We can go case by case, but it would be confusing if you had some will-change for some set of properties that in some combinations should cause certain things and we don't capture that
<fantasai> ... In this case we know the answer
<oriol> q+
<kbabbitt> fantasai: you're kind of generalizing the principle, right flackr?
<kbabbitt> flackr: yes
<kbabbitt> fantasai: will-change z-index won't have an effect if we're statically positioned, but proposal is that it does create a stacking context, because if position were something else it would
<JohnJansen> ack oriol
<fantasai> oriol: My preference would be for the opposite, which firefox chrome and servo implement
<fantasai> ... if you specify z-index, then it only has an effect if z-index applies
<fantasai> ... it's true that we can imagine some future cases of combinations of propertis that would be more complex
<fantasai> ... but it's hypothetical, and still doable
<fantasai> ... so I have a mild preference is that the effect only applies when the reference property applies
<fantasai> flackr: disagree that doable in the future
<fantasai> ... we can't assume the greatest impact if it changes this case right now
<fantasai> ... we're saying today that will-change: z-index won't apply a stacking context unless positioned, we can't change that in the future
<emilio> I think this relates to the issue we discussed last week right?
<fantasai> oriol: I wasn't saying about changing this decision
<fantasai> ... but about more complex issues that could occur in the futue
<emilio> What does will-change: transform do if you put it on a non-transformable element?
<fantasai> flackr: Right, it doesn't prevent us from doing other combinations in the future

<kbabbitt> fantasai: two competing positions, flackr is saying will-change z-index should always create a stacking context, oriol is saying it should only create a stacking context only incases where it *could*
<kbabbitt> ... I think I lean towards oriol's position
<dbaron> (BTW, I think fantasai is correct that position doesn't actually create a stacking context, since I think it only creates pseudo-stacking-contexts.)

<kbabbitt> ... it would be weird to have side effects of properties ... if properties that only applied in flex created a stacking context, would we have it create a stacking context always even if we aren't in flex?
<kbabbitt> ... do we ahve to look at what they could to in any mode before we decide they wont ever apply?
<kbabbitt> ... seems kind of weird
<kbabbitt> q+
<kbabbitt> ... could potentially be confusing because z-index also creates a stacking context in grid
<JohnJansen> ack kbabbitt
<fantasai> kbabbitt: was going to ask the same question emilio raised
<fantasai> ... also to fantasai's point
<fantasai> ... we went through this exercise of trying to take existing grid properties and applying to grid lanes layout
<fantasai> ... we were successful
<flackr> q+
<fantasai> ... but if we decide that once a property could create a stacking context, will-change will always create stacking context, could that block some similar unification effort in the future
<JohnJansen> ack flackr
<fantasai> flackr: I'm not opposed to taking the resolution that it only applies based on current set of properties on the element
<kbabbitt> fantasai: if they're both listed, then yeah
<fantasai> ... then we can consider in the future the set of properties that will-change, can any values on those sets, would that cause
<dbaron> (though according to css-position-3 sticky and fixed create stacking contexts (though CSS 2.1 didn't say that for fixed)
<kbabbitt> ... if any combination would create the effect, then we can create the effecet
<kbabbitt> ... but if position is not listed, authors are not expecting it ro
<fantasai> s/ro/to change... idk

<fantasai> PROPOSED: will-change: z-index only creates a stacking context if either a) it currently could have that effect if its own value changed or b) it could have an effect if some combination of the properties in will-change changed

<fantasai> RESOLVED: will-change: z-index only creates a stacking context if either a) it currently could have that effect if its own value changed or b) it could have an effect if some combination of the properties in will-change changed

<dbaron> ok, chromium code at https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/style/computed_style.cc;l=2958-2995;drc=7e10886d92c5a02e5876cd873716caf580a437f7 agrees with css-position-3 so Simon is correct that this case is ok
<fantasai> flackr: I think we agree for ? they're the same thing
<flackr> s/?/stacking context
<fantasai> RESOLVED: Only keep (a) above, leave (b) for future discussion

resolutions.background: I think a `hanging` value for `text-box-edge` would be useful, as in some fonts, the `cap` and `text` baselines don't suffice to trim to the hanging line. For example, when trimming the "Shurjo" font on [this Bengali news site](https://www.prothomalo.com/) with `text-box-trim`, I get the following results on Chrome and Safari (as well as Firefox with my WIP `text-box-trim` implementation). The `te
irc: <kbabbitt> fantasai: somebody requested to add hanging for text-box-edge
<kbabbitt> ... hanging is a baseline that's supposed to correspond to the top edge of this line drawn across the indic scripts

<kbabbitt> ... I think that it makes a lot of sense to do this, kind of sort of, one consideration I have is I'm not clear if hanging baseline represents top edge of that top line or middle of that top line
<kbabbitt> ... if you have multiple blocks you're tyring to line up, what do Indic users expect to happen?
<kbabbitt> ... if it's top edge of top line, then it would make a lot of sense to set this to text box edge
<kbabbitt> ... if not we might need a slightly different definition
<kbabbitt> ... we have a bunch of issues around text box edge for non line scripts not having the metrics they need
<jfkthame> q+
<kbabbitt> ... this is one of them
<JohnJansen> ack jfkthame
<kbabbitt> jfkthame: I think it would make sense for the hanging baseline to be at the top edge of the head line that goes across the script
<dbaron> I would hope that the baseline is the top edge of the line, by analogy with the alphabetic baseline typically being at the bottom edge of lines.
<kbabbitt> ... thinking about cases I've seen where there is a mix of sizes
<kbabbitt> ... think of a drop cap type of situation
<kbabbitt> ... what I've seen in cases like that is the top edge of the glyph ink gets aligned
<kbabbitt> ... so that's what's meant by hanging
<kbabbitt> fantasai: ok, in that case I think it would make sense to add this value
<kbabbitt> ... and we'll naturally run into the problem that fonts don't usually specify it
<astearns> +1 to adding this
<fantasai> PROPOSED: Add hanging value to text-box-edge
<fantasai> RESOLVED: Add hanging value to text-box-edge
<dbaron> this is presumably to the first half of the 2 value syntax?
<fantasai> yes
<dbaron> and its to the <text-edge> production?

resolutions.resolution: rule-visibility applies per segment even in grid lanes
resolutions.background: The `rule-visibility-items` properties control whether gap decoration segments are painted next to empty areas.
irc: <fantasai> javierct: want to define rule-visibility items for grid lanes
<fantasai> ... controls whether gap decorations get painted next to empty areas
<fantasai> ... in grid-lanes containers we can have empty tracks
<fantasai> ... My proposal is that we have rule-visiblity items only affect cases with empty tracks
<fantasai> ... if you have rule-visibility between, only paint between non-empty areas
<fantasai> ... then no decorations get painted because segments are between non-empty areas
<fantasai> ... so if track is non-empty, then we count it as having content
<fantasai> ... vs if it's empty then we don't have content and we determine the behavior
<fantasai> ... relates to other issue, if we look at grid lanes diagram with intersection
<fantasai> ... right now it's per-gap-decoration-segment
<fantasai> ... we have those orange segments
<fantasai> ... current algorithm would test emptiness on each individual segment
<fantasai> ... we have multiple segments in the same gutter
<fantasai> ... so doesn't make sense to do what I'm proposing
<fantasai> ... because looking at each segment created in the grid axis
<fantasai> ... if in the grid axis we decide there's only one segment
<fantasai> ... then follows very simply, if something in other track, then can easily decide whether to draw
<fantasai> ... but if we have multiple disjoint segments, doesn't line up with what's in the spec, and then might be harder to define
<alisonmaher> q+
<kbabbitt> fantasai: you have multiple segments even if we adopt the proposal we can have spanning items
<kbabbitt> ... a segment above the spanner and below the spanner
<kbabbitt> ... if there's no content after the spanner, that should count as empty for the content after the spanner, so you still have that problem
<JohnJansen> ack alisonmaher
<fantasai> alisonmaher: We did previously resolve that flexbox doesn't support rule-visibility
<kbabbitt> ... if that's what we resolved for flex then resolving the same for grid-lanes probably makes sense
<kbabbitt> ... I guess grid-lanes has explicit placement whereas flexbox doesn't, is that the situation alisonmaher?
<fantasai> alisonmaher: two precedents, flex and multicol
<fantasai> ... multicol considers it
<fantasai> ... and flexbox ..
<fantasai> ... so what does this mean for grid lanes
<JohnJansen> q?
<fantasai> ... I suggest making it similar to multicol
<fantasai> ... that seems clearer precedent to follow
<kbabbitt> fantasai: for multicol, what happens if you have a spanner?
<kbabbitt> fantasai: some text, a spanner, more text that appears only in the first column but not the second
<fantasai> javierct: in that case, say you choose between, we wouldn't paint decoration below the spanner
<fantasai> ... because the segment below the spanner, there's a segment there, and content on only one side
<kbabbitt> q+
<fantasai> ... so we end up with rule-visility items between, content on both sides of segment
<JohnJansen> ack kbabbitt
<fantasai> kbabbitt: So in that case, what Elika suggested, rule-visibility taking effect per segment would be consistent
<fantasai> ... which makes sense to me
<fantasai> javierct: agree
<fantasai> PROPOSED: rule-visibility applies per segment even in grid lanes
<fantasai> javierct: would that mean, on other issue, outside of spanner case, we don't have those intersections?
<kbabbitt> fantasai: I think you can go either way, they're independent questoins
<kbabbitt> ... if we make it per segment, rules are more complicated to implement, but to the extent we have multiple segments, having it makes sense
<kbabbitt> ... question is, what is a segment?
<fantasai> javierct: I was thinking more about tracks
<fantasai> ... if we want to do per segment, rather than per track
<fantasai> ... that's fine
<fantasai> ... just means we keep as is
<fantasai> RESOLVED: rule-visibility applies per segment even in grid lanes

resolutions.resolution: Adopt :disabled styles in the issue (with some selector munging)
resolutions.background: Splitting out from https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14254: refining color adjustments used to communicate form control states:
irc: <masonf> that one?
<fantasai> s/Topic/Subtopic/
<fantasai> i/Subtopic/Topic: Form Control Styling/
<masonf> nicole: disabled states are important for communicating inertness
<masonf> ...cursor behavior plus colors
<masonf> ...wanted to make as much contrast as possible, while still communicating disabled.
<masonf> ...contrast rules for disabled controls aren't required to hit normal WCAG
<masonf> ...for high contrast mode, we increased the contrast, but it's hard.
<masonf> ...hard to disambiguate disabled and other controls.
<masonf> ...typography is the hardest to change without making it too close to regular color (maybe clickable).
<keithamus> q+
<masonf> fantasai: disabled colors currently damp down color to 50%. Propose add background color of 6% currentcolor
<masonf> ...to preserve contrast. Raise disabled color from 50 to 55%. Also since we reduced border color, also reduce border color from 50% to 25%.

<fantasai> :is(select, input, textarea):disabled { /* Overrides all interactivity styles from above */ color: color-mix(currentColor 55%, transparent);              /* previously 50% */ border-color: color-mix(currentColor 25%, transparent);       /* previously 50% */ background-color: color-mix(currentColor 6%, transparent);    /* previously transparent */
<astearns> ack keithamus
<fantasai> }
<masonf> keithamus: no particular objections, seems reasonable. Curious: any research indicating these states are represented by anything other than color?
<masonf> nicole: yes. cursor value changes
<masonf> keithamus: anything else?
<masonf> ...touchscreen - only thing is color, right?
<bkardell> contrast?
<Luke> q+
<masonf> keithamus: I'm in forced colors on a touchscreen, how can I tell it's disabled?
<masonf> nicole: if you try to interact, nothing happens.
<masonf> keithamus: disabled form controls aren't focusable.
<masonf> fantasai: if you click or hover, nothing happens.
<kbabbitt> q+
<masonf> keithamus: curious if there are other signals, but sounds like no. This is fine otherwise.
<masonf> nicole: we tried iconography for error state, and it doesn't work well, especially in other languages and writing modes.
<masonf> ...tried for a long time and wasn't able to make it not look broken.
<astearns> ack Luke
<masonf> Luke: other than tweaking of selectors, this looks good to me.
<masonf> ...forced colors mode questions remain. There's likely a precedent there.
<Ameer> present-
<masonf> ...using color as the only way isn't ideal, for keyboard users they can't focus, AT users get told they're disabled, so mainly it's touchscreen.
<masonf> ...I think that's ok. Clicking it and finding it doesn't do anything is ok - it's non-destructive.
<masonf> q+
<masonf> ...specifics of how you've done it: is this how design systems do this today?
<masonf> nicole: yes, design systems use shades of grey for form controls in general. They aren't dealing with some of the complexities of currentcolor
<masonf> ...they use the lightest possible colors, and we are going the other way. Prioritizing user needs is more important.
<astearns> ack kbabbitt
<masonf> kbabbitt: q about background color: when discussing popover for select, we were doing that with shadows.
<masonf> ...in dark mode could it send the same signal, use light dark?
<masonf> nicole: yes. I may not have done dark mode
<masonf> ...dark mode - because we lighten the color to pull it forward, we need to lighten it less in dark mode.
<masonf> jensimmons: if you disable controls, background comes up. In dark mode...
<Luke> Placeholder is TBD
<masonf> keithamus: placeholder on textarea - might be a bug
<masonf> nicole: no research on placeholders. Hard to distinguish it from text the user has typed. Come back to that.
<Luke> q+
<masonf> kbabbitt: we're using a similar signal for popup vs. disabled, but it seems fine.
<masonf> jensimmons: tricky - there are many states, hard to make them distinct
<fantasai> scribe+
<astearns> ack masonf
<keithamus> q+
<fantasai> masonf: Generally, I think this looks good.
<fantasai> ... I do want to make sure we do the forced colors and prefered contrast
<fantasai> fantasai: Yes, plan to do that next
<fantasai> masonf: Coming back to touchscreen, my sense from working on interest invokers, is that it's a user discover
<fantasai> ... you get a hint from the color maybe, but you find out by tapping on it

resolutions.resolution: Leave flex as-is; grid lanes TBD
resolutions.background: Currently, the segment endpoint algorithm creates "internal" endpoints at a gap junction, which according to the spec:
irc: <fantasai> javierct: Says that segment ? are at gap junctions
<fantasai> ... Has different implications per layout model
<kbabbitt> s/?/endpoints/
<fantasai> ... multicol is very simple, just between columns
<fantasai> ... grid has intersections so endpoints at intersections
<fantasai> ... flex creates endpoints at gap junctions
<fantasai> ... ends up with internal segment end points
<fantasai> ... for grid lanes, similarly only tracks in one axis
<fantasai> ... so we end up with gutters between tracks
<fantasai> ... and then internal gutters within each track
<fantasai> ... problem is that, per spec, endpoint behavior makes it so that in the grid-axis gap (between tracks), when we have junctions we create endpoints just like in flex
<fantasai> ... with rule-break: intersection, end up with uneven breaking in the lines between tracks
<fantasai> ... creates a weird jagged line
<fantasai> ... propose instead that we treat it more as we do multicol and grid (?), where we don't treat stacking-axis gutters as abutting grid-axis gutters
<fantasai> ... this way we don't end up with internal endpoints
<fantasai> ... instead, we don't break at all (Except for spanners)
<kbabbitt> q+
<fantasai> ... This is what happens in multicol without rows
<fantasai> ... rule-break becomes continuous
<fantasai> ... so we'd change language in the spec so that we don't imply that the gutters in the stacking axis are abutting those in the grid axis
<fantasai> ... and we don't end up with so many internal endpoints
<fantasai> zakim, start meeting
<Zakim> inviting RRSAgent
<Zakim> RRSAgent, make logs Public
<Zakim> Meeting: Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) Working Group Teleconference
<RRSAgent> logging to https://www.w3.org/2026/09/30-css-irc
<RRSAgent> I have made the request, Zakim
<fantasai> kbabbitt: I support this change, and honestly think we should do the same in flex
<fantasai> ... behavior that flex decorations break at intersections was an attempt to break like grid
<fantasai> ... but admittedly it looks weird
<fantasai> ... when you have two items that end near each other, it greats a weird elongated gap
<kbabbitt> https://drafts.csswg.org/css-gaps-1/images/flex-negative-gap-decoration-segments.png
<fantasai> ... same thing can happen in grid lanes
<fantasai> ... so suggest we do what javier suggests
<kbabbitt> scribe+ kbabbitt
<JohnJansen> q?
<JohnJansen> ack kbabbitt
<JohnJansen> ack fantasia
<kbabbitt> fantasai: strongly agree we should keep flex and grid-lanes consistent
<JohnJansen> ack fantasai
<kbabbitt> ... do we have rule-break independently for each axis?
<fantasai> javierct: We don't
<fantasai> kbabbitt: Yes we do!

<kbabbitt> fantasai: so what if instead of ... if the author really wants it to break at intersections ... for flex there's often a behavior where people will not, if not inherently grid-like, people will size the items as if they were a grid
<kbabbitt> ... in that case you wouldn't be able to get intersection behavior at all

<kbabbitt> ... would it make sense to have some kind of distinction between intersection being only for non-main in flex and grid-lanes by default but make it possible for authors to get it if they wanted to?
<fantasai> javierct: Default is normal, and that doesn't look like breaking at intersections
<kbabbitt> fantasai: what happens by default in flex or grid-lanes?
<fantasai> javierct: rule-break is normal, which breaks only at spanning items
<fantasai> ... if you wanted to change that, you could set 'intersection'
<fantasai> ... but otherwise would onl break at spanning items
<kbabbitt> fantasai: and how would that be different from what you're proposing?
<fantasai> javierct: I would disallow the current rule-break behavior in grid lanes
<kbabbitt> fantasai: but what's the difference in behavior you're proposing between intersection and normal?
<fantasai> javierct: There would be no difference between 'intersection' and 'normal'
<fantasai> javierct: similar to regular multicol, if no column wrap
<kbabbitt> fantasai: multicol I think, talking about it without the wrap doesn't make sense, because there is no secondary axis
<kbabbitt> ... so it doesn't make sense to compare this to multicol
<kbabbitt> ... it's a single row of items
<kbabbitt> ... is the behavior with normal that's what we expect people to want, is there a point to disabling 'intersection'?
